title: Observer Grammar
description: The shared descriptive sequence used to document an observer from phenomenon through claim boundary.

nodes.label: Phenomenon
nodes.description: The physical, computational, conceptual, or unknown subject being observed.
nodes.claimBoundary: The phenomenon is distinct from its representation.

nodes.label: Field
nodes.description: The carrier or structure through which the phenomenon is expressed.
nodes.claimBoundary: A declared field model is not a broad physical conclusion.

nodes.label: Transport
nodes.description: The declared evolution or propagation toward an observer.
nodes.claimBoundary: Implemented transport and analogy must remain distinct.

nodes.label: Interaction
nodes.description: The event at the sensing boundary or interaction region.
nodes.claimBoundary: Selection effects and losses remain explicit.

nodes.label: Receiver
nodes.description: The biological, optical, instrumental, or computational component that records an interaction.
nodes.claimBoundary: Shared receiver vocabulary does not imply shared mechanisms.

nodes.label: Measurement
nodes.description: The recorded quantity with declared units, range, calibration, and channel semantics.
nodes.claimBoundary: Different measurement channels require an explicit comparison basis.

nodes.label: Artifact
nodes.description: The persistent object that preserves the measurement or its representation.
nodes.claimBoundary: An artifact preserves evidence within its recorded provenance and scope.

nodes.label: Interpretation
nodes.description: The stated reasoning that connects an artifact to a bounded conclusion.
nodes.claimBoundary: Direct reading, inference, analogy, and speculation remain labeled.

nodes.label: Claim Boundary
nodes.description: The explicit supported, inferred, and unknown limits of the entry.
nodes.claimBoundary: No observer entry is complete without this boundary.

groups.label: Observer Grammar Sequence
groups.description: All required grammar nodes in descriptive order.

claimBoundary: Shared grammar does not imply shared physics or measurement equivalence.
